rationale: C11 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s central argument: education is principally a local community responsibility; citizens should meet to study school problems and act on them; and the Federal Government should assist without controlling education. The child compresses this same machinery and philosophy into its account of locally representative participants studying science and mathematics teaching, developing practical solutions, and turning to government only when necessary. C14 closely reinforces the conference-and-local-control pattern, while C04 shares the science-and-engineering problem/action framing but less of the child’s distinctive structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The dynamic drive for better schools and better education will come from men and women--representing all the aspects of American life--sitting down together, studying the problems that confront them, working out practical solutions
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Under this program, half a million citizens met in almost 4,000 communities across the country to study and act on the problems of their schools.
shared_material.explanation: Both make organized local citizen deliberation and action on school problems the central mechanism for educational improvement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: turning to government only for that which they themselves cannot accomplish at all or so well
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the role of the Federal Government is to aid, encourage, and facilitate-but never to control--education
shared_material.explanation: The child restates C11’s limited-support conception of federal involvement in education.

shared_material.child_excerpt: we naturally tend to emphasize the need for expansion and improvement in our science and mathematics programs. But in no way do we ignore the constant need and the permanent values of general education
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a special problem results from the increasing impact of scientific development on our lives and the international competition in this development... I have therefore acted to encourage the training of more scientists, engineers and technicians.
shared_material.explanation: Both place expanded scientific training within a broader national education policy, though the child adds an explicit defense of general education.
